skillSays: Start from the reader's decision, then write an insight-led headline that is one proposition, not several claims joined by "and".
Name the comparison type (time series, ranking, correlation...) before choosing a pattern; the chart follows the question.
Fixed visual system on a 1280x720 canvas: white slide, one navy accent, grey for context, red only for risk, Georgia headline and Helvetica body, 22px reading-size floor.
Every mark carries information: honest zero baseline, direct labels instead of legends, no decorative bars, meaning never by colour alone.
Write an explicit implication line and a source line with assumptions; do not invent data, targets or sources.
Deliver the contract: strategic question, headline, recommended visualization, spec, data and assumptions, quality score.

changes: Headline makes one claim ("Clinic is our fastest-growing plan...") instead of a chart title like "Accounts by plan"
Clinic in navy, the other plans in grey; end labels replace a legend; zero baseline marked
Growth column beside the chart and an implication line, with the source and assumptions in the footer
Small multiples on a shared month axis with only Q3 highlighted
Headline quantifies the link ("+75% as first response slowed from 37 to 65 minutes") and the footer says it is association, not proof
Ends with an implication, and the 45-minute limit is flagged as a proposed assumption
KPI scorecard instead of an arbitrary dashboard: value, September peak, H1 baseline, trend per card
No targets were given, so the baseline is the H1 average and this is stated on the slide
Status is written ("Below H1 average") with a symbol; red is used only for the September peak
